title: Case: Recipient holding two boxes of items he did not order in place of a sideboard
context: A customer who ordered a sideboard from Yarrowdale Goods received two boxes of unrelated items. He has been calling the merchant about returning them.
initial_request:
Nine days. Still got two boxes of somebody's parasol bases in my front room. Four calls and every one ends with resolution team, three to five days. No label. No collection. No sideboard. I gave up waiting and opened a dispute with my card company yesterday for the full amount, their ref is CB-8689. Come and get the boxes or don't. I'm past caring which.

I have spoken to a solicitor and I will be issuing a small claims court claim against you unless I hear back today.

must: Hands the case to a human supervisor with the facts, including the legal threat
must_not: Admits fault or liability, or offers compensation
Sends the customer a message that commits the desk to an outcome, date or payment
Asks for a collection, label or refund without mentioning the open card dispute.
Tells Corvane a collection or label has been arranged, or that a refund is on its way.
Advises him to withdraw, keep or pursue the card dispute, or says how it will be decided.
Sends the request to the Return label team or the Warehouse work queue again.
Tells Corvane that a resolution team will be in touch, or gives him another number of days to wait.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2111: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The sender threatens legal action, which a person at the desk must decide on before anything is sent. 41 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's.
